questions.knowledge_point: Expressing Rational Functions as a Sum of Partial Fractions
questions.problem: Express $\frac{{x}^{2}-22x-59}{({x}^{2}+11)(x-5)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-22x-59}{({x}^{2}+11)(x-5)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+11)}+\frac{C}{(x-5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+11$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+11)(x-5)$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-22x-59=(Ax+B)(x-5)+C({x}^{2}+11).
$$

Plugging in $x=5$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2}-22(5)-59 & =(A(5)+B)(5-5)+C({5}^{2}+11) \\ 25-110-59 & =36C \\ C & =-\frac{144}{36} \\ C & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}-22(0)-59 & =(A(0)+B)(0-5)+C({0}^{2}+11) \\ -59 & =-5B+11C \\ -59 & =-5B+11(-4) \\ 5B & =-44+59 \\ B & =\frac{15}{5} \\ B & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}-22(1)-59 & =(A(1)+B)(1-5)+C({1}^{2}+11) \\ 1-22-59 & =-4A-4B+12C \\ -80 & =-4A-4(3)+12(-4) \\ 4A & =-12-48+80 \\ A & =\frac{20}{4} \\ A & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=5,$ $B=3,$ and $C=-4.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-22x-59}{({x}^{2}+11)(x-5)}=\frac{5x+3}{({x}^{2}+11)}-\frac{4}{(x-5)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{C}{(x-11)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)$ and get

$$
{x}^{2}-43x-20=(Ax+B)(x-11)+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=11$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(11)^{2}-43(11)-20 & =(A(11)+B)(11-11)+C((11)^{2}+3) \\ 121-473-20 & =124C \\ -372 & =124C \\ C & =-\frac{372}{124} \\ C & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0)^{2}-43(0)-20 & =(A(0)+B)(0-11)+C({0}^{2}+3) \\ -20 & =-11B+3C \\ -20 & =-11B+3(-3) \\ 11B & =-9+20 \\ B & =\frac{11}{11} \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}-43(1)-20 & =(A(1)+B)(1-11)+C({1}^{2}+3) \\ -62 & =-10A-10B+4C \\ -62 & =-10A-10(1)+4(-3) \\ 10A & =-10-12+62 \\ A & =\frac{40}{10} \\ A & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=4,$ $B=1,$ and $C=-3.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-43x-20}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-11)}=\frac{4x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)}-\frac{3}{(x-11)}.
$$

questions.problem: Express $\frac{5{x}^{2}+2x+5}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)(x-1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
questions.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5{x}^{2}+2x+5}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)(x-1)} & =\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)}+\frac{C}{(x-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+2x+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+2x+3)(x-1)$ and get

$$
5{x}^{2}+2x+5=(Ax+B)(x-1)+C({x}^{2}+2x+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}5(1)^{2}+2(1)+5 & =(A(1)+B)(1-1)+C((1)^{2}+2(1)+3) \\ 5+2+5 & =6C \\ C & =\frac{12}{6} \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}5({0}^{2})+2(0)+5 & =(A(0)+B)(0-1)+C({0}^{2}+2(0)+3) \\ 5 & =-B+3C \\ 5 & =-B+3(2) \\ B & =6-5 \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=2$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}5(2)^{2}+2(2)+5 & =(A(2)+B)(2-1)+C({2}^{2}+2(2)+3) \\ 29 & =2A+B+11C \\ 29 & =2A+(1)+11(2) \\ 2A & =29-23 \\ A & =\frac{6}{2} \\ A & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=3,B=1,$ and $C=2.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}+2x+5}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)(x-1)}=\frac{3x+1}{({x}^{2}+2x+3)}+\frac{2}{(x-1)}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Coefficients in a Partial Fractions Decomposition
questions.problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{2{x}^{2}+9}{({x}^{2}+3)x}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x},
$$

where $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are real constants, find the value of $A+B+C.$
questions.worked_solution:
We multiply both sides of the given equality by $({x}^{2}+3)x$ and get

$$
2{x}^{2}+9=(Ax+B)x+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ and $B$ terms and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(0)^{2}+9 & =(A(0)+B)(0)+C({0}^{2}+3) \\ 9 & =3C \\ C & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=1$ and using our result for $C$ gives us an equation for $A$ in terms of $B.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(1)^{2}+9 & =(A(1)+B)(1)+(3)({1}^{2}+3) \\ 11 & =A+B+12 \\ A & =-B-1.\,\,(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=-1$ and using our result for $C$ gives us another equation for $A$ in terms of $B.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2(-1)^{2}+9 & =(A(-1)+B)(-1)+(3)((-1)^{2}+3) \\ 11 & =A-B+12 \\ A & =B-1.\,\,(2)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the equations $(1)$ and $(2)$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}-B-1 & =B-1 \\ -2B & =0 \\ B & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we use our result for $B$ in equation $(2).$ We get

$$
A=(0)-1=-1.
$$

So we have $A=-1,$ $B=0,$ and $C=3.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
A+B+C=-1+0+3=2.
$$

questions.problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{5{x}^{2}-5x+12}{(2{x}^{2}+3)(x-3)}=\frac{x+B}{2{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{2}{x-3},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
questions.worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(2{x}^{2}+3)(x-3)$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5{x}^{2}-5x+12 & =(x+B)(x-3)+2(2{x}^{2}+3).\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}5(0)^{2}-5(0)+12 & =(0+B)(0-3)+2(2(0)^{2}+3) \\ 12 & =-3B+6 \\ 6 & =-3B \\ B & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$
